project: RFP - Enterprise Work Order Management System

criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: Nine tabs, every card drills to a detail page; all content read at runtime through assets/js/data.js. The published plan.json has no requirements, measures, guardrails or systems and placeholder dates, so those tabs show empty states and Overview > Plan check lists the gaps; plan.json was not edited. The Data model tab renders a proposal from knowledge/data-model.json and looks requirement statements up in plan.json. Run `npm test` (23 tests).

criteria.text: Given a new work order, when I create it, then it should appear in the system with GIS data.
Given an existing work order, when I update it, then the changes should be saved and reflected in the GIS data.
Trust: Given any work order action, when it is performed, then an audit trail entry must be created.

stories.notes: Verified against a STAND-IN GIS (server/gis/stand-in-assets.json): no access to the city GIS yet. The real GIS plugs in behind createGisClient() with the same getAsset/linkWorkOrder methods. Create, update and complete each write their audit entry in the same transaction; GIS write-back is queued in gis_sync and retried if GIS is down. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo`.

criteria.text: Given a work order update, when saved, then the GIS database reflects the changes.
Given a GIS update, when processed, then the work order reflects the changes.
Trust: All GIS interactions are logged with timestamps.

stories.notes: Verified against the STAND-IN GIS (no city GIS access yet). Work order -> GIS: queued write-back from STORY-001. GIS -> work order: processGisChanges() polls numbered changes, applies each with its audit entry and cursor in one transaction. Every GIS call goes through createGisClient, which requires a logger and writes one gis_log row per attempt. Credential comes only from GIS_TOKEN; unauthorized is not retried. The demo reads the stand-in directly for display only. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo`.

criteria.text: Given a citizen request, when submitted, then it appears in the work order system.
Given a public work order, when viewed, then it shows current status and history.
Trust: All public submissions are logged with timestamps and IP addresses.

stories.notes: Public page at /public and endpoints under /api/v1/public. A submission creates a service request and a work order (via STORY-001 createWorkOrder, actor public-portal) and returns a tracking code. Every submission attempt, including unreadable and rate-limited ones, is logged with time and IP in the staff-only public_submission_log; IPs cleared after a PLACEHOLDER 90 days. Work orders are private until staff publish them (publishWorkOrder); there is no staff screen for that yet. Runs locally only (GitHub Pages cannot run the server). Run `npm test`, `npm run demo:public`, `npm run public`.

criteria.text: Given an API request, when received, then the system processes it according to specifications.
Given a data update, when via API, then it reflects in the system.
Trust: All API interactions are logged with timestamps and request details.

stories.notes: Generic, specified API connection for outside systems: create/update/complete work orders under work_orders:write, bodies checked against the OpenAPI contract (generated from the same field lists), ETag/If-Match versioning (412 on stale, 428 if missing), Idempotency-Key per system, and an api_request_log row for every request (field names only, never values or keys). Proven with a SIMULATED external system; REQ-054 coordination with specific vendors is still to be done by people (see STORY-009). Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:external`.

criteria.text: Given work order data, when analyzed, then the system generates a heat map.
Given a heat map, when viewed, then it accurately reflects work order distribution.
Trust: All heat map generations are logged with parameters and timestamps.

stories.notes: Grid heat maps (50 m - 2 km cells) by work type, date and status at GET /api/v1/heat-maps (scope heatmaps:read, never public), as GeoJSON for the city GIS or an SVG image without a street map. Work orders without coordinates (own or citizen pin) are counted as unmapped; cell counts + unmapped always equal the matching total. Every generation attempt (ok, invalid, failed) is in heat_map_log; refused requests are in the audit trail and request log. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:heatmap`.

criteria.text: Given a workflow change, when applied, then the system supports the new workflow.
Given an existing workflow, when reviewed, then it operates as expected.
Trust: All workflow changes are logged with user IDs and timestamps.

stories.notes: Versioned workflows per work type: named steps with allowed next steps, exactly one final step. The built-in Standard workflow (Open -> Completed) is today's behaviour and covers every work type without its own, so existing work is unchanged. A change is published as a new version; work orders keep the version they started on. Definitions that could strand work orders (dead ends, unreachable steps, no way to finish, unknown steps, duplicates) are refused with every problem listed (422) and nothing saved. Publish and retire need workflows:admin; moving a work order (POST /api/v1/work-orders/{id}/transition, If-Match) needs work_orders:write; completion still needs a note. Every publish, retire and move is audited with user and time. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:workflows`.

criteria.text: Given a user role, when assigned, then the user has appropriate access.
Given a user action, when performed, then it is logged in the audit trail.
Trust: All access changes are logged with user IDs and timestamps.

stories.notes: Staff users with roles (six PLACEHOLDER built-in roles whose permissions are the existing API scopes) and personal keys (hwu_..., hash only, shown once). A person's permissions are re-read from their roles on every request, so granting or removing a role takes effect at once; if they cannot be read, the key can do nothing. Administrators (access:admin, with their own key - system keys are refused) add users, grant/remove roles and issue/revoke keys at /api/v1/users; the last active administrator cannot lose the role. Every audit entry made in a person's request carries their verified user id; acting under another name is refused and audited; refusals are audited. Auditors read GET /api/v1/audit (audit:read) by user, item, action and time; reading it is audited. Workflow steps can require a role, now enforced. Run `npm test`, `npm run demo:access`; first administrator: `npm run admin:bootstrap`.

criteria.text: Given a system setting, when configured, then it applies across the system.
Given a user account, when managed, then changes reflect immediately.
Trust: All configuration changes are logged with user IDs and timestamps.

stories.notes: System settings defined in code (type, range, default) with the city's values in system_settings: public rate limit, IP retention days, vendor review overdue days, default heat map cell size. Each is read when used, so a change applies on the next request. Changes (PUT/DELETE /api/v1/settings/{key}, settings:admin, personal key, If-Match) are saved with their audit entry and read back; out of range -> 400, stale -> 412, not confirmed -> 503 configuration_not_saved. User management: edit (If-Match), deactivate (key removed, refused next request; not yourself, not the last administrator), reactivate (new key needed); city-defined roles from known permissions, changes apply at once, built-in roles fixed, in-use roles cannot be deleted. Everything audited with user id and time; refusals audited, including system keys. Run `npm test`, `npm run demo:settings`.

criteria.text: Given a vendor API, when integrated, then data exchange is seamless.
Given a data request, when via API, then it is processed correctly.
Trust: All vendor API interactions are logged with timestamps and request details.

stories.notes: One-way vendor feeds per the RFP (REQ-042: LAMA, SpryPoint, Madison AI one-way; REQ-055: no current interface, should be API): GET /api/v1/vendors/{vendor}/feed, each vendor with its own key and its own versioned contract - Madison AI the full agreed read format, Lama and SpryPoint a PROPOSED minimal set with no free text or names. Records are checked against the contract before sending (mismatch -> 500, nothing sent); cursor always returned so a vendor resumes with only what changed. Every request (ok, denied, invalid, mismatch, error) is in vendor_exchange_log with times, parameters and request id; if it cannot be logged nothing is sent. REQ-054: npm run vendor:check conformance kit (timeouts, capped retries, no retry on refused keys) and a per-vendor coordination tracker (contract shared, fields confirmed, sandbox tested, signed off; in order, audited, people only). HONEST STATE: no real vendor has connected; the Lama and SpryPoint field lists await vendor confirmation; SCADA (REQ-042) not built. Run `npm run demo:vendors`.

criteria.text: Given system configuration, when assessed, then it meets operational standards.
Given a readiness checklist, when completed, then the system is ready for launch.
Trust: All readiness assessments are logged with timestamps and reviewer details.

stories.notes: Readiness assessment against the July 1, 2027 go-live date: 11 automatic checks (settings valid, an administrator who can sign in, workflows completable, audit trail writable, a create/update/complete smoke test on a throwaway database, GIS and Blue Stakes queues clear, GIS and Blue Stakes live with a recent successful call, Lama/Sprypoint/Madison AI each with a recent successful exchange) and 10 manual items for configuration, testing and data conversion that a project manager records (not applicable needs a reason). Verdict ready only if every item passes; a crashing check counts as failed. Each assessment is kept with reviewer, times and every result and audited; if it cannot be recorded, no result (503). readiness:review, personal key, Idempotency-Key. HONEST STATE: today's real system is NOT READY (stand-in GIS and Blue Stakes, no vendor integrations - STORY-009 is waiting on vendor coordination - and no manual sign-offs); 'ready' is shown with a fully prepared example. Run `npm run demo:readiness`.

criteria.text: Given the system's database, when accessed by Madison AI engines, then it should allow indexing and searching of work order data.
Given a request from Madison AI, when it queries the API, then it should receive the correct data format.
Trust: Given any data access by Madison AI, when it occurs, then it must be logged in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Madison AI reaches work order data through an audited, read-only HTTP API (list, changes-since, search, get one) rather than direct database access, as agreed with the student, so every access can be logged. Proven against our published OpenAPI contract and a SIMULATED Madison AI crawler; Madison AI's own spec and credentials are not available yet. Fails closed: no audit entry means no data. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:api`.

criteria.text: Given a requirement, when a vendor submits compliance documentation, then it should be stored in the system.
Given a technical approach, when a vendor submits it, then it should be reviewed and approved.
Trust: Given any vendor submission, when it is received, then it must be logged in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Vendor portal as API endpoints under /api/v1/vendor (no web page yet). Submissions with documents are stored with their audit entry, read back and fingerprint-checked inside the transaction before a receipt is returned; every submission received - stored, duplicate or refused - is in the audit trail. Reviewers approve or request changes (comment required, not their own organisation); review queue flags items waiting over a PLACEHOLDER 5 days. Requirements catalog copied from the STORY-000 brief because plan.json has none. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:vendor`.

criteria.text: Given a Bluestakes data entry, when I update the data, then the system reflects the changes accurately.
Given a Bluestakes data entry, when I mark it as complete, then the system updates its status to complete.
Trust: Given a Bluestakes data entry update, when the update is made, then the system logs the change in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Locate tickets from Blue Stakes are imported, updated, answered and completed, each audited in the same transaction. Verified against a STAND-IN Blue Stakes feed and client with PLACEHOLDER response codes; no Blue Stakes access yet. Exposed as API endpoints that need the locate_tickets:write scope; refusals are audited. Per-person logins come with STORY-007. Also fixed a flaky STORY-011 test (tests/madisonApi.test.js). Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:tickets`.

criteria.text: Given work orders exist, when the console loads, then each row shows status, assignee and location.
Given a work order is opened, when the detail view renders, then its full history and GIS record appear on one screen.
Given no work orders exist, when the console loads, then an empty state is shown rather than an error.
Given the console is deployed, when it is opened at 1440x900, then every screen renders without a horizontal scrollbar so it can be captured for the proposal exhibit.
Trust: every action taken in the console writes to the same audit trail as the API, recording who did it and when.

stories.notes: Staff console at /console: a person signs in with their personal key and gets a session (30 min idle, 8 h max) that acts as them, in the same audit trail as the API. Criteria: rows show status, assignee and location (tests/consoleViews.test.js:36); detail shows full history and the live GIS record on one screen, with the saved copy if GIS is down (consoleViews.test.js:77, :98); no work orders gives an empty state, not an error (consoleViews.test.js:55); every screen fits 1440x900 with no horizontal scrollbar, checked in headless Edge (tests/consolePages.test.js:51, npm run console:check); console actions are audited with who and when (tests/consoleSessions.test.js:76). Built in commit b1e7b56. Run `npm test` and `npm run console`.

criteria.text: Given an incoming citizen request or Bluestakes record, when it is received, then a draft work order is proposed with its fields already filled in.
Given a proposed draft, when I approve it, then the work order is created and the record names who approved it.
Given a proposed draft, when I edit or reject it, then my version is what is saved and the original proposal is retained.
Given the approval queue, when it renders, then each item states who performs the work and who must approve it.
Trust: no work order reaches a live queue without a named person approving it, and the screen shows who that was.

stories.notes: AI-first intake: citizen requests and Blue Stakes tickets arrive as drafts from the intake agent (a labelled rule-based stand-in until an AI model is provided); a named person with intake:approve approves, corrects or rejects each one in the console (#/intake). Criteria: a request or Blue Stakes record arrives as a filled-in draft (tests/intakeDrafts.test.js:27, :42); approving creates the work order and names the approver (tests/intakeReview.test.js:42, tests/intakeHttp.test.js:57); an edit or rejection saves my version and keeps the original proposal (intakeReview.test.js:56, :68); the queue states who performs the work and who must approve (intakeHttp.test.js:43); Trust: nothing reaches the live queue without a named person, and the screen shows who (intakeReview.test.js:142, intakeHttp.test.js:125). Failure paths: undetermined field (intakeReview.test.js:80), two approvers at once (:92), source changed (:115). Built in commit 27ca901. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:intake`.

criteria.text: Given work orders with locations, when the map loads, then each one is plotted at its GIS coordinates.
Given a date range is selected, when the heat map renders, then it reflects only work orders within that range.
Given the GIS source is unavailable, when the map loads, then it says so and still lists the work orders.
Trust: the map reads the same GIS record as the API, so what is displayed and what is stored cannot disagree.

stories.notes: Map and heat map in the staff console (#/map, heat layer #/map?heat=1) over GET /api/v1/console/map. Criteria: each work order with a location is plotted at its coordinates, and one without is listed with the reason (tests/mapView.test.js:31); a date range shows only work orders in that range: the map uses the heat map's own filters and always counts the same work orders (mapView.test.js:41), and the heat map's date filter is proved in tests/heatMaps.test.js:78-90; an empty range is an empty result, not an error (mapView.test.js:50); GIS unavailable: the map says so and still shows every work order from the stored record (mapView.test.js:75); Trust: GIS confirms each linked position and a moved asset is flagged, never silently moved (mapView.test.js:57), and the HTTP map returns exactly what mapPoints gives (mapView.test.js:89). Grid map with no street basemap (that would need an outside tile service). Built in commit 1a742c2. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:map`.

criteria.text: Given I am an administrator, when I open the console, then I can view and change user roles and system settings.
Given I am not an administrator, when I open the console, then I am refused and the refusal is recorded.
Given any change is made, when I open the audit trail, then that change appears with actor, timestamp and previous value.
Trust: the console enforces the same role checks as the API, so no screen can grant what the API would refuse.

stories.notes: Administration console (#/admin/users, roles, settings, audit) over the existing access, settings and audit APIs, with no permission logic of its own. Criteria: an administrator views users, roles and settings and changes a role and a setting (tests/adminConsole.test.js:45); a non-administrator is refused on every administration screen and each refusal is recorded with who tried (adminConsole.test.js:65, :76); every change appears in the audit trail with actor, time and previous value (adminConsole.test.js:123); Trust: a supervisor's session cannot grant roles, change settings or deactivate anyone, nothing changes and every attempt is recorded (adminConsole.test.js:86). Failure paths: the last administrator cannot remove their own role (:99); a user who no longer exists gives 404 (:109); an audit trail longer than one page is paged without skipping or repeating (:138). Built in commit b1656bc. Run `npm test` and `npm run demo:admin`.

criteria.text: Given configured integrations, when the view loads, then each shows its vendor, status and the time of its last successful call.
Given an integration has failed, when the view loads, then it is flagged with the error class and the time it began failing.
Given the readiness checks, when the view loads, then each check shows pass or fail with the evidence behind it.
Trust: every status shown is read from a real call result, never from a stored flag that nothing updates.

stories.notes: Integrations & readiness screen in the staff console (#/integrations), over GET /api/v1/console/integrations and POST /api/v1/console/integrations/{name}/check (readiness:review). Criteria: each integration shows vendor, status and last successful call (tests/integrationStatus.test.js "every configured integration", tests/integrationsConsole.test.js "a project manager sees"); a failing one shows its error class and when it began failing (integrationStatus.test.js "a failing integration", integrationsConsole.test.js "when GIS is down"); each readiness check shows pass or fail with its evidence, and done-with-no-note shows as no evidence (integrationStatus.test.js "after an assessment", "marked done with no evidence"); Trust: every status is worked out from the call logs (gis_log, bluestakes_log, vendor_exchange_log, integration_checks) on each request, never stored (integrationStatus.test.js "the status follows the latest real call", "no status is stored"). A GIS reply that succeeds with the wrong shape is flagged unexpected_payload. Vendors are one-way (they call us), so their status comes from their feed requests; Blue Stakes has no read-only call, so no Check now. All 17 console screens fit 1440x900. Run `npm test`, `npm run demo:integrations` and `npm run console`.
